title: TS SDK: unify AsyncIterator and Web Streams ergonomics for streaming responses
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Consumers currently face friction choosing between AsyncIterator and Web Streams in the TS SDK. Different calling patterns, inconsistent backpressure semantics, and subtle retry interactions mean examples are duplicated across docs and users struggle to implement robust resume/retry logic. Goal: provide one ergonomic surface that interoperates seamlessly with AsyncIterator and Web Streams, documents clear retry semantics for streaming partial responses, and ships examples for common runtimes (Node 18+, Deno, browser).
rationale: We want a single mental model for streams in the SDK. AsyncIterator is ergonomic for typical Node code and easy for for-await loops; Web Streams are required for fetch-based streaming in browsers and for middleware that expects ReadableStream. Ensuring convertibility and consistent behavior across both reduces docs burden and prevents user errors (e.g., accidentally double-consuming a stream or losing resume tokens during retry).
design_decisions: Expose a top-level StreamResponse that implements AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array> and has a .toWebStream() helper for Web Stream consumers.

Standardize chunk envelope to include: {type: 'data'|'meta'|'done', delta?: string|Uint8Array, resume_token?: string, trimmed?: boolean}. This keeps binary/text parity and lets retries attach resume tokens.

Backpressure: keep SDK-initiated buffering minimal (one chunk buffer) and rely on underlying runtime's stream backpressure. When converting to AsyncIterator, support a configurable internal queue with a maxQueueLength option (default 4) to avoid memory blowup for high-throughput workloads.

Retries: implement idempotent append protocol where server-provided resume_token is authoritative. On transient error, SDK will pause consumption, attempt up to N retries (configurable; default 3), and re-open a stream with ?resume_token=...; during retry the AsyncIterator/WebStream remains usable and will continue yielding once connection resumes.
Cancellation: calling .return() on the AsyncIterator or closing the Web Stream's controller will immediately signal the runtime to cancel and emit a final 'canceled' meta chunk to telemetry.

Errors: non-transient server errors surface as iterator throw()/stream error. Partial yield semantics are preserved (previously yielded chunks remain), calling code is responsible for application-level reconciliation.
Testing: use cross-runner harness to validate Node streaming, browser fetch streaming, and Cloudflare Workers environment. Include deterministic mock server for resume-token behavior.
migration_notes: Existing APIs that returned Node Readable or raw Response.body should be deprecated in favor of StreamResponse. Provide an adapter helper .fromLegacyReadable() during a 1 release deprecation window.

User code using for-await loops should continue to work; default queue sizes may change behavior in pathological high-throughput loops — call out in changelog and provide knob to restore previous behavior.
Docs will include a migration recipe for explicit retry handling if users implemented custom resume semantics prior to server-provided resume_token.
testing_plan: Unit tests for iterator<>WebStream conversion ensuring no data duplication or loss across conversion boundaries.
Integration test using mock server that injects transient 500 errors and validates SDK reopens with resume_token and yields remaining data exactly once.
E2E smoke tests in Node 18 and latest Chromium for browser streaming harness.
Load test with synthetic high-QPS streams to validate in-process queueing and memory boundedness (heap should remain within target for 1M tokens/min test).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes StreamResponse with AsyncIterator and .toWebStream().
Interoperability tests pass: converting iterator->WebStream and WebStream->iterator yield identical chunk sequence and metadata.
Retry flow: after N transient network failures, stream continues from resume_token without duplicate or missing chunks in integration harness.
Cancellation semantics tested: .return() and controller.close() trigger a single cancellation side-effect (telemetry event + server cancel request).
Docs and three example recipes (Node, Browser fetch, Deno) merged to docs repo and referenced in PR.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge API and tests behind feature flag 'ts_stream_unified' for SDK nightly builds.
2) Publish beta SDK (2.4.0-beta.1) and link examples in quickstart.
3) Monitor errors and memory signals for 2 weeks; opt-in customers given guidance to test their workloads.
4) Flip feature flag, publish stable 2.4.0 and announce migration notes in changelog and dev newsletter.
